title: Finite trials reduced short-lag link recovery in two passive adult worm circuit models
abstract: We tested finite-trial link inference in two passive electrical models from partial adult C. elegans maps. Each model had 180 cells, equal independent current noise and 90 observed cells. Ten observation masks and ten sampling replicates per mask used exact Gaussian sample cross products from independent stationary triplets. At 10,000 trials and lag 0.01, forward covariance curvature gave mean precision at the known link count of 0.0062 and 0.0083. Static inverse covariance gave 0.9917 and 0.9818. Curvature had perfect population ranks in all masks at this lag. Even at 100 million trials, its mean precision was only 0.5370 and 0.5248. Lag 0.1 reduced sampling error but left map-dependent bias. An exact Gaussian variance formula gives leading score variance proportional to 1/(N h^3). Independent numerical checks support the sampling calculation. These results limit this estimator in this model benchmark, not all inference methods. Independent trials, known mean and edge count, assumed conductance and noise, incomplete maps and no recorded activity limit use. Code, aggregate scores, a figure, source hashes and separate-data retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Mean precision at the known observed link count versus independent trial count. Lines compare curvature and inverse covariance at two lags. Bands give the range of ten mask means, each from ten sampling replicates. These are not biological confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Uses its model, cell rule and exact-covariance benchmark as prior context. New code tests finite independent trial samples.
